prompt: Some people argue that primary schools focus too much on formal learning. To what extent do you agree with this opinion? How important do you think it is for children to play as well as learn in the primary school classroom?
essay:
Nowadays, many argue that schools only focus on formal ways to learn, and many people are discussing the importance of children to play as well as learn in primary school. I definitely agree with the idea that most primary schools only concentrate on conventional and specific ways of learning

Many teachers place importance on formal learning, too much methodology, with a strict system, strict exams, with rankings with all the other children and not enough practice. Namely, a large part of minors have disabilities or difficulties adapting to college for the first time. For example, in France, the education minister placed additional courses on the weekend to offer educational games, to help them with reading, counting, listening, etc...

It is clear that it is essential to play and learn in the primary school classroom, because there is no special age. In addition, a part of the students’ needs requires specific attention, and a special way to study. For instance, in the United States, the government established the law A-52 in 2024, by which citizens whose children were in certain educational places  underwent a trial called "Let's protect our infants". The results gave rise to creating some rules to offer the opportunity to some people with specific needs, also adapting their way of teaching with some games, and finally, specific programs, adapted to every child.

To conclude, I believe that today, schools are prioritising a simple and only way to study, which is very precise, strict and complex. Furthermore, some people need specific games to understand easily. In my opinion, it is essential to consider the needs of every kid studying.
